answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the spiral: one wallet must post equal stake on every chain it claims. The vine links these stakes into a single identity root, so splitting across chains costs N× the capital for N chains. An attacker farming 20 chains faces 20× locked value with no added yield — the anchor holds one identity per stake cluster, and returns go negative before chain five. This works because binding makes sybil cost scale linearly with breadth while rewards stay flat.
